Cover letter
6 November 2026
Editor-in-ChiefBiomedical Engineering / Biomedizinische Technik
Re: Research Article — Fixed-threshold transfer and equal-review ranking in breast ultrasound segmentation quality control
Dear Editor-in-Chief,
We request consideration of this manuscript as a Research Article. It examines two operating questions in breast ultrasound segmentation quality control: transferring a development-calibrated numerical review threshold and selecting a fixed number of cases by risk ranking.
A frozen SAM ViT-B generated shared initial masks for confidence and prompt-disagreement scores in a reference-informed, known-location setting. Each score targeted 20 % review in 213 BUS-BRA development patients; the cutoffs were transferred to 851 internal and 252 BrEaST external patients. Detection, actual review fractions and missed low-quality masks were evaluated jointly.
The confidence threshold selected 20.45 % of internal patients and 13.89 % externally. Relative detection counts changed between transferred cutoffs and equal review at the 20 % target; a complete eight-budget analysis showed no uniformly better score. The revised manuscript uses this distinction to explain how an operating rule changes the interpretation of score comparisons. Three bootstrap routes and descriptive diagnostic-stratum accounting characterize its sampling and case-mix context without changing the prespecified H1–H3 analyses.
Actual prediction contours are supplied for all six audited external misses. A targeted CPU replay used checkpoint bytes identical to the original and preserved every review and quality label, with numerical differences disclosed. The reference-derived prompts define a known-location evaluation, and review flags are simulated counts rather than measured reader time.
The authors report no research funding or conflicts of interest. OpenAI Codex assistance is disclosed in the manuscript and original Ethical and Legal Declarations form. The authors previously confirmed statutory ethics-review exemption under Article 32 of the Chinese Measures (2023).  Both authors have approved the final manuscript, supplementary materials and figures for submission to Biomedical Engineering / Biomedizinische Technik and accept responsibility for the entire content. The work is original and is not under consideration by another journal. Earlier manuscript drafts and supporting research materials are publicly available in our GitHub repository: https://github.com/khkh87885-code/research.
Sincerely,Haoze Lan, corresponding authorOn behalf of Haoze Lan and Ziyuan Zhu
